intro.tagline: An interactive 3D petri dish and microbiology lab simulator.
intro.placeholderNote: Early build: one dish, one organism, loop streaking and time controls. This page will become the full introduction and instructions.
intro.disclaimer: Agar is an educational model. It is not a substitute for real laboratory work.

tools.title: Tool
tools.handHelp: Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, right-drag to pan.
tools.loopHelp: Drag on the agar to streak. Right-drag to orbit.
tools.swabHelp: Drag on the agar to spread a lawn, or swab the whole plate at once.

hints.discTooClose: Too close to another disc or to the edge. Keep discs 24 mm apart.
hints.notOnBench: Bring the plate back to the bench first.
hints.benchFull: Four plates is the limit. Discard one first.

escherichia-coli.fact: A gut bacterium and the workhorse of molecular biology. Ferments lactose, so it grows pink to red on MacConkey agar.

staphylococcus-aureus.fact: Golden colonies of cocci in grape-like clusters. Beta-hemolytic on blood agar and turns mannitol salt agar yellow.

staphylococcus-epidermidis.fact: A harmless resident of human skin. White colonies, no hemolysis, and no colour change on mannitol salt agar.

bacillus-subtilis.fact: A spore-forming soil bacterium. Its colonies are dry, dull and wrinkled with an irregular edge; a frequent airborne contaminant.

pseudomonas-aeruginosa.fact: Flat, spreading colonies with a metallic sheen. Releases a blue-green pigment that soaks into the agar, and smells of grapes.

serratia-marcescens.fact: Famous for its blood-red pigment, prodigiosin, which it makes at room temperature but not at body temperature.

micrococcus-luteus.fact: Slow-growing, bright yellow colonies of cocci in tetrads. Lives on skin and dust and often lands on open plates.

chromobacterium-violaceum.fact: A soil and water bacterium whose colonies are deep violet from the pigment violacein.

proteus-mirabilis.fact: So motile that it swarms across the agar in waves, leaving concentric rings instead of separate colonies.

streptococcus-pyogenes.fact: Tiny grey colonies of cocci in chains, each surrounded by a wide, completely clear zone of beta-hemolysis.

streptococcus-pneumoniae.fact: Lancet-shaped cocci in pairs. Small glistening colonies with a greenish zone of alpha-hemolysis.

klebsiella-pneumoniae.fact: A thick capsule makes its colonies large, domed and slimy. Ferments lactose: pink and mucoid on MacConkey agar.

salmonella-enterica.fact: A motile enteric rod that does not ferment lactose, so its colonies stay colourless on MacConkey agar.

candida-albicans.fact: A yeast, not a bacterium: large oval cells that bud. Cream, pasty colonies that prefer Sabouraud agar.

penicillium-chrysogenum.fact: The blue-green mold behind penicillin. Velvety colonies with a white growing edge that inhibit nearby bacteria.

aspergillus-niger.fact: A fast mold that starts white and turns black as its spore heads form.

rhizopus-stolonifer.fact: Black bread mold. Cottony growth that can fill a whole plate in two to three days.

nutrient-agar.name: Nutrient agar
nutrient-agar.about: General-purpose medium; most non-fastidious organisms grow.

lb-agar.name: LB agar
lb-agar.about: Rich general-purpose medium, the standard for E. coli work.

blood-agar.name: Blood agar
blood-agar.about: Enriched with sheep blood; shows alpha, beta or gamma hemolysis.

macconkey-agar.name: MacConkey agar
macconkey-agar.about: Selects Gram-negative enterics; lactose fermenters turn pink.

mueller-hinton-agar.name: Mueller-Hinton agar
mueller-hinton-agar.about: Standard medium for antibiotic disc testing.

sabouraud-agar.name: Sabouraud dextrose agar
sabouraud-agar.about: Acidic, sugar-rich; favours yeasts and molds.

mannitol-salt-agar.name: Mannitol salt agar
mannitol-salt-agar.about: High salt selects staphylococci; mannitol fermenters turn it yellow.
